name: Expected annual loss from natural hazards, $ a year
plain: How much money natural hazards are expected to cost each municipio in an average year, by FEMA's model.
definition: FEMA's estimate of the average loss each year, in dollars, to buildings, agriculture and lives (lives valued in dollars by FEMA's rule), from the 18 hazards of the National Risk Index.

coverage.frequency: One snapshot: the National Risk Index version of December 2025. Renewed with each full build (python environment_series.py).

method: environment_series.py reads FEMA's county table of the National Risk Index for Puerto Rico's 78 municipios and publishes the expected annual loss as given; Puerto Rico's value is their sum. It also checks that the composite risk score, social vulnerability and community resilience are still empty for Puerto Rico and records it in the file's notes.
source_detail: FEMA National Risk Index (December 2025), county table: EAL_VALT and HRCN_EALT, ERQK_EALT, IFLD_EALT, LNDS_EALT, CFLD_EALT, TSUN_EALT
how_to_read: $3.19 billion a year for Puerto Rico; the most in San Juan $434,520,246, Bayamón $167,313,545, Carolina $154,370,865. The Analysis tab shades it per resident, so large municipios do not dominate.
caveats: A model estimate of average loss, not a record of what was lost.
FEMA's composite risk score, social vulnerability and community resilience are empty for Puerto Rico; this file does not fill them.

name: Landslides mapped after Hurricane María (2017)
plain: How many landslides geologists mapped in each municipio after Hurricane María.
definition: Slope failures (landslides, debris flows and rock falls) that USGS and UPRM geologists mapped from aerial images taken after Hurricane María, by the municipal boundary that holds each one.

coverage.frequency: One storm: the slope failures mapped after Hurricane María (September 2017).

method: environment_series.py reads the 71,431 mapped points and places each one in the municipal boundary that holds it (all of them fall inside one). The copy's own municipio and barrio names are not used.
source_detail: Hughes and others (2019), USGS data release doi:10.5066/P9BVMD74, read from the first author's copy at UPRM (DERRUMBES_HURACAN_MARIA): point locations only
how_to_read: 71,431 for Puerto Rico; the most in Utuado 17,762, Maricao 5,806, Jayuya 4,874: the steep, wet centre-west of the island.
caveats: A record of one storm, not a forecast of where slides will happen.
Read from a copy of the USGS data release kept by its first author at UPRM, because the USGS catalogue refuses scripts.

name: Wetlands, km²
plain: How much of each municipio is wetland: marshes, swamps, mangroves and tidal flats.
definition: The area of the wetlands the National Wetlands Inventory maps in the municipio: estuarine and marine wetlands (mangroves, beaches, tidal flats), freshwater marshes and freshwater swamps and shrub wetlands, in square kilometres. Lakes, ponds, rivers and open water are left out.

coverage.frequency: One snapshot of the inventory, read in October 2026; almost all of the wetland area lies in the parts mapped from aerial photographs of 1983 (the coasts).

method: environment_series.py reads the inventory's polygons of Puerto Rico from its map service and keeps the three wetland types (estuarine and marine wetland, freshwater emergent, freshwater forested and shrub). Each polygon is split among the municipal boundaries in metres (NAD83 Puerto Rico); the part beyond the drawn coast goes to the municipio with the largest share. Mangroves are the polygons coded E2FO3 or E2SS3.
source_detail: USFWS National Wetlands Inventory map service, layer Wetlands: ATTRIBUTE, WETLAND_TYPE and the outline; photo years from the Data_Source service
how_to_read: 488.27 km² for Puerto Rico; the most in Lajas 38.5 km², Loíza 35.9 km², Cabo Rojo 24.8 km².
caveats: Almost all of the wetland area was mapped from aerial photographs of 1983: wetlands filled or restored since then are not shown.
Areas are worked out from the inventory's outlines and can differ from official acreages.

name: Residents with no risk factors, % (Community Resilience Estimates)
plain: Out of every 100 residents of each municipio, how many have none of the Census Bureau's disaster risk factors.
definition: Residents with none of the risk factors, in percent of the residents the estimates cover. The risk factors are the Census Bureau's ten risk factors that make it harder to withstand and recover from a disaster: household income below 130% of the poverty line, only one or no adults aged 18 to 64 in the household, more than 0.75 people per room, limited English or no one with a high-school diploma in the household, no one employed full-time year-round, a disability, no health insurance, age 65 or over, no vehicle and no broadband.

coverage.frequency: One release a year: 2019, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024 (no release for 2020).

method: environment_series.py reads each release's Puerto Rico municipio file and the island row of its tract file and publishes the three shares (PRED0_PE, PRED12_PE, PRED3_PE) with their margins of error (_PM, 90% confidence).
source_detail: Census Bureau Community Resilience Estimates for Puerto Rico, files CRE{yy}_PR_MUNICIPIO.csv and CRE{yy}_PR.csv, 2019 and 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024
how_to_read: Puerto Rico: 14.74% in 2019 and 18.09% in 2024 (± 0.55 points). Highest in 2024: Dorado 27.0%, Guaynabo 26.5%, Barceloneta 24.3%.
caveats: Modelled estimates with margins of error: read the margin before comparing two places.
The ten factors are the same in every release, but from 2023 the Census Bureau computes municipio margins a new way (smaller), so compare margins across 2022 and 2023 with care.

One factor is a household where no one speaks English very well (or no one has a high-school diploma), so in Puerto Rico it counts many Spanish-speaking households and raises the shares with risk factors.

name: Earthquakes of magnitude 2.5 or more
plain: How many earthquakes of magnitude 2.5 or more struck in or just off each municipio, every year.
definition: Earthquakes of magnitude 2.5 or more in USGS's catalogue whose epicenter is in the municipio or, offshore, nearest to it and within 25 km of its coast.

coverage.frequency: Whole calendar years. The last two years are downloaded again with each full build.

method: environment_series.py asks ComCat for every earthquake of magnitude 2.5 or more in a box around Puerto Rico each year. An earthquake counts in the municipio whose boundary holds its epicenter; offshore, in the nearest municipio if it is within 25 km of that municipio's coast, else not at all. Each earthquake counts once, so the municipal values add up to Puerto Rico's.
source_detail: USGS ComCat event web service (fdsnws/event/1), format csv, minmagnitude 2.5, latitude 17.4-19.0, longitude -68.4 to -64.9, 2000-2025: epicenter and magnitude
how_to_read: Puerto Rico: 153 in 2000, 6,297 in 2020 (the southwest sequence; strongest 6.4) and 522 in 2025.
caveats: A count of events, not of damage: most are felt little or not at all.
The catalogue records more small earthquakes in later years as the seismic network grew.
